title: 37.3 Monolithic in-Memory Computing Microprocessor for End-to-End DNN Inferencing in MRAM-Embedded 28nm CMOS Technology with 1.1Mb Weight Storage
problem: DNN inference on always-on AI sensors requires ultra-low power during both computation and idle phases; prior in-memory computing (IMC) works focused only on individual crossbar arrays, insufficient for complete DNNs.
motivation: Always-on AI sensors demand sparse inference with minimal power consumption; MRAM-based IMC offers non-volatile weight storage with low idle power and high endurance, but scaling beyond individual arrays to full DNN inference is undemonstrated.
method: Neural networks need to repeatedly perform matrix multiplications, which normally requires fetching weights from distant storage—a power-hungry process for always-on sensors. This microprocessor integrates magnetic memory (MRAM) directly on-chip to store 1.1 megabits of weights right next to the compute hardware. The MRAM cells form crossbar arrays (grids where current flows through magnetic cells), performing multiply-and-add operations directly in the hardware using analog electrical signals. Because weights are stored co-located with the math, the entire neural network can run without fetching data from external memory, eliminating a major source of power consumption.
key_novelty: First microprocessor to demonstrate end-to-end deep neural network inference with all weights stored on-chip in MRAM-embedded 28nm CMOS technology.
contributions: Low idle and compute power via non-volatile MRAM
limitations: Abstract-only; model accuracy, DNN topology/layer support, inference throughput, latency, and power breakdown (compute vs weight fetch) not quantified.
primary_theme: Monolithic MRAM-based in-memory computing for complete DNN inference
